title: Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE)
author: Neilier Junior
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9b7h2rn
materials: Put running buffer in the bowl halfway.

steps.title: Prepare Separation Gel Buffer (150 mL)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1.5 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.8 buffer.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 27.23 g Tris (18.15 g/100 mL) in 80 mL diH2O.
Adjust pH to 8.8 using HCl.
Bring final volume to 150 mL with diH2O.
Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Stacking Gel Buffer (100 mL)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0.5 M Tris-HCl, pH 6.8 buffer.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 6.00 g Tris in 60 mL diH2O.
Adjust pH to 6.87 with HCl.
Bring final volume to 100 mL with diH2O.
Store at 4 °C.
Add 10.00 g SDS to 90 mL diH2O.
Solubilize the SDS.
Bring final volume to 100 mL with diH2O.

steps.title: Prepare 10% Ammonium Persulphate (APS) (1 mL)
steps.instruction: Prepare 10% APS fresh at time of use.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 0.10 g APS in 1 mL diH2O.

steps.title: Prepare 10x Running Buffer (1 L)
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of 10x Running Buffer (approx. pH 8.3; do not adjust pH).

substeps.instruction: Combine 30.30 g Tris base, 144.10 g Glycine, and 10.00 g SDS in diH2O to reach a final volume of 1 L.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Buffer (8 mL)
steps.instruction: Prepare 2X Sample Buffer (62.5 mM Tris-HCl pH 6.8, 25% glycerol, 2% SDS, 0.01% bromophenol blue).

substeps.instruction: Combine 1.0 mL 0.5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 6.8), 2.0 mL 25% glycerol, 0.08 mL 1.0% bromophenol blue, 1.6 mL 10% SDS, and 2.92 mL diH2O.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Plates
steps.instruction: Clean and assemble the electrophoresis equipment.

substeps.instruction: Clean workbench, glass plates, spacers, combs, and other equipment with alcohol.
Assemble the plates.
Apply a thin layer of Vaseline to the rubber of the mounting bracket.
Check for leaks by adding water, then fully remove water with filter paper.

steps.title: Cast the Separation Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the separation gel (volumes standardized for two 7 cm wide, 1.5 mm thick gels).

substeps.instruction: Choose the required concentration of separation gel and separate two erlenmeyers (one for separation gel, one for stacking gel).
Prepare the separation gel solution.
Add TEMED just before pouring.
Pour the solution onto the plate up to the demarcated limit for the stacking gel.
Apply a thin layer of n-butanol over the gel to level the upper portion (do not leave in contact for more than 1 h).
Keep the polymerization cassette level and wait for complete polymerization.
Remove n-butanol and wash with water; dry well.

steps.title: Cast the Stacking Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the stacking gel onto the polymerized separation gel.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the stacking gel solution.
Add TEMED and apply the stacking gel to the separation gel.
Immediately insert the comb, ensuring no bubbles are trapped.
Wait for full polymerization.
Optional: Store gel overnight in running buffer at 5 °C.
Calculate sample volume to provide ≈ 30 µg protein per channel.
Distribute calculated volume into 600 µL microtubes.
Add 2X sample buffer at a 1:1 ratio. (If using 4X buffer, use 3:1 ratio: 5 µL buffer, add sample, and complete with diH2O to 30 µL for 1.5 mm gel).
Boil the mixture at 100 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Set Up and Run Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load samples and run the gel at 200 V.

substeps.instruction: Attach plates to the support (gel plate and dead plate).
Fill the space between plates with ≈ 30 mL running buffer and check for leaks.
Remove the comb.
Apply samples to respective channels; fill empty channels with sample buffer.
Fit electrodes and run at 200 V (Expected current: initial 35-50 mA, final 20-31 mA).
Stop the run when bromophenol blue reaches the lower limit of the gel (do not let it escape completely).

steps.title: Fix the Gel
steps.instruction: Fix the proteins in the gel.

substeps.instruction: Remove the gel from the plates and mark the left and right sides.
Place the gel in a fixative solution (10% methanol, 5% acetic acid) and stir for 2 h.

steps.title: Option A: Silver Staining
steps.instruction: Perform silver staining to visualize proteins.

substeps.instruction: Discard fixative solution.
Perform three 10-min washes with 50% ethanol (92% commercial ethanol acceptable).
Incubate with 0.02% sodium thiosulphate solution for 1 min.
Wash with distilled water 3 times.
Incubate in silver nitrate solution (0.2 g silver nitrate, 0.037 mL 37% formaldehyde, 100 mL water) for 20 min.
Wash with water 3 times for 20 s each.
Apply developer solution (2 g sodium carbonate, 1 mL 0.02% sodium thiosulfate, 0.025 mL 37% formaldehyde, completed to 50 mL with water).
Once bands reach the required standard, stop the reaction by adding 3 mL acetic acid.

steps.title: Option B: Coomassie Staining
steps.instruction: Perform Coomassie staining to visualize proteins.

substeps.instruction: Discard fixative solution.
Prepare Coomassie solution: Dissolve 100 g ammonium sulfate (10%) and 1 g Coomassie G250 (0.1%) in 400 mL water until sulfate dissolves.
Slowly add 20 mL phosphoric acid (2%) followed by 200 mL methanol (20%).
Add the remaining 400 mL of water.
Add the completed solution to the gel.
